purpose: Replace schematic-heavy presentation with recorded simulations and released multi-seed statistical charts.
benchmark_source: Unmodified top-level V3 results in the supplied tmc_project archive; SHA-256 values match the earlier README benchmark_summary.json.
simulation_source: Supplied source/checkpoint; Joint / seed 0 / Full MPC / default SimConfig; Source Only and CTTA newly recorded on CPU; existing CAMPE replay independently rerun and exactly matched.
time_convention: step=-1 is the initial state at t=0; step j>=0 is recorded after its transition, at (j+1)*0.5 s.

charts.tracking_comparison: Three raw radial-error traces; initial state included in lines; episode means exclude step=-1. One illustrative episode per method, not multi-seed averages.
charts.evolution_heatmap: Ten logged/derived signals from post-step CAMPE records. Each row is min-max normalized over all 300 steps, without smoothing. Speeds are finite differences of positions divided by dt; per is the logged EMA estimate. This uses the same mechanism-view idea as Fig. 7, not an exact reproduction of its normalized curves.
charts.radial_error_histogram: One value per episode (radius_error), 40 released episodes for each of Source Only, CTTA and CAMPE. Fixed 0.25 m bins from 0 to 4 m; every observation is included. The animation adds matched seed-scenario rows, not mission time.
charts.benchmark_heatmap: Two views: 6 methods x 4 structured regimes and 4 methods x 10 OOD scenarios. Each cell is 10-seed medium-profile success percentage; shared 0-100 scale; reveal order is presentation only.
charts.aoi_distribution: Empirical cumulative distribution of episode-mean aoi for Fixed USV, FIM Only, Dual-Plane and Full MPC (50 episodes each); a subset of the six planners in Table IV, explicitly named. Animation scans the AoI threshold, not simulation/training time.

statistical_scope: Plots show empirical data, not population guarantees. Histograms/ECDFs show distributions, not confidence intervals; correlations or aligned traces do not by themselves identify causal effects.
